title.value: PARTIAL MODELS FOR BUILDING ADAPTIVE MODEL-BASED REINFORCEMENT LEARNING AGENTS
title.justification: The title of the research paper is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of the document.
title.quote: P ARTIAL M ODELS FOR B UILDING A DAPTIVE M ODEL -B ASED R EINFORCEMENT L EARNING A GENTS

analysis.description: This paper discusses the use of partial models in deep model-based reinforcement learning to enhance local adaptivity of agents. By deploying multiple models for different parts of the state space, the study shows that adaptive behavior to local changes in the environment can be achieved in agents like deep Dyna-Q, PlaNet, and Dreamer.

type.justification: The paper conducts experiments with deep reinforcement learning agents using various setups (MountainCarLoCA, MiniGridLoCA, ReacherLoCA, etc.) to demonstrate the effectiveness of partial models in achieving local adaptivity.
type.quote: We demonstrate the effectiveness of partial models by first instantiating them in the deep Dyna-Q agent and showing that they allow for achieving local adaptivity on the Local Change Adaptation (LoCA) setup (Van Seijen et al., 2020; Wan et al., 2022) of both the MountainCar and MiniGrid domains.

name.justification: The paper focuses on advancing adaptive behavior in model-based reinforcement learning through the use of partial models.
name.quote: In reinforcement learning, however, recent studies have shown that modern model-based agents display poor adaptivity to such changes.
